newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W. Australia unions step up campaign against IR Bill.
newsitem.headline: W. Australia unions step up campaign against IR Bill.

text.p: A strike by building workers at the A$575 million Collie power station construction site in the south-west of Western Australia was only the first stoppage in protest at proposed industrial relations legislation, a union official said on Wednesday.
"(The campaign) is going to go on and on," said Joe McDonald, state secretary of the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Workers' Union (CFMEU).
"There are going to be many, many stopages over this."
McDonald said about 400 building workers on the Collie site walked off this morning and will stay out until Monday.

The action is directed against the state government's Labour Relations Amendment Bill which includes provisions requiring pre-strike secret ballots and banning the use of membership fees for political campaigns.
It is the second time the Court government has attempted to introduce pre-strike secret ballots. The first attempt foundered in the face of widespread industrial action.

The latest protest campaign again has wide support within the trade union moment. The Maritime Union of Australia was reported today to have endorsed industrial action "of the nature not seen for years", and health workers at major Perth hospitals are meeting this week to discuss joining the protest.
CFMEU members at Kwinan, Muchea and Bunbury power stations have also voted to support the protest.
However, the president of the CFMEU's mining and energy division, Ron Keilty, told Reuters today no decision had yet been made on when industrial action in the power industry would begin.
Meanwhile the Chamber of WA Commerce and Industry (CCI) revealed its appeal to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) to get involved had failed.
CCI Director of Operations, Brendan McCarthy, said the CCI had called on the AIRC to intervene under Section 127 of the Workplace Relations Act.
"We've only just received the response and we will be looking at our options later today," McCarthy said.
"But we are extremely disappointed to say the least. Here is a body established specifically to prevent disputes but it is loath to prevent a major dispute in Western Australia."
